title: Vendor Management Policy
body:
Vendor Management Policy
Owner: Catherine Hale, Chief Executive Officer
Last updated: 2026-09-08

Purpose
This policy sets out how Halcyon Ridge Capital selects, onboards, monitors, and exits third-party vendors. Our trading, wealth, lending, and advisory businesses rely on external data, infrastructure, and service providers. A failure at a vendor can become a failure at the firm, so every vendor relationship needs a named internal owner and a documented risk assessment.

Scope
This policy applies to every external organization that provides goods or services to the firm, or that touches firm systems or data. Examples include market data and pricing vendors feeding MarketDataFeed and PricingSvc, sanctions list providers supporting SanctionsScreen, payment network and bank connectivity providers behind PaymentsGateway, cloud and hosting providers, identity providers connected to AuthSSO, and outside consultants and contractors. It applies to all employees in all teams.

Roles and Responsibilities
Business Owner: The head of the team that sponsors the vendor. The Business Owner is accountable for the relationship, the business case, and the annual review.
Technology: Sam Okafor, Director of Engineering, or a delegate reviews technical integration, access scope, and architecture fit for any vendor connecting to a firm system.
Risk: Owen Gallagher, Head of Risk, assigns the vendor tier and signs off on concentration and operational resilience risk.
Compliance: Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer, reviews regulatory, sanctions, AML, and data protection exposure.
Operations: Ravi Patel, Head of Operations, owns payment, settlement, and reconciliation-related vendors and verifies service levels against operational procedures.
Finance: Martin Osei, Chief Financial Officer, approves spend and reviews contract terms with material financial commitments.
COO: Linda Brandt maintains the central vendor register and chairs the quarterly Vendor Oversight Review.

Vendor Tiering
Every vendor is assigned one of three tiers before contract signature.
Tier 1 (Critical): The vendor supports a critical system, or an outage would halt trading, settlement, payments, or regulatory screening. Examples are providers for MarketDataFeed, SanctionsScreen, PaymentsGateway, and AuthSSO.
Tier 2 (Important): The vendor supports a standard system or handles confidential firm information, for example providers connected to DocVault, DataLake, or ClientHub.
Tier 3 (Low): No system access, no confidential data, and easy substitution.
The tier drives the depth of due diligence and the monitoring frequency described below.

Due Diligence
Before engagement, the Business Owner submits a vendor request through the procurement workflow. Required reviews:
1. Financial health review, including audited statements for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors.
2. Information security assessment, including independent audit reports where available and evidence of access controls, encryption, and incident response.
3. Compliance screening covering sanctions, adverse media, and ownership.
4. Business continuity and disaster recovery review, including tested recovery objectives for Tier 1 vendors.
5. Dependency mapping by Technology showing which firm systems and downstream systems rely on the vendor. For example, a pricing vendor failure affects PricingSvc, and therefore RiskEngine, OMS, TradeBlotter, and PortfolioMgr.
Tier 1 vendors also require Risk to document a fallback or substitute plan.

Contract Requirements
All Tier 1 and Tier 2 contracts must include: defined service levels with remedies, right to audit, breach notification within 24 hours of discovery, data return and deletion on termination, subcontractor disclosure, confidentiality terms, and regulatory cooperation clauses. Legal review is mandatory. No employee may sign a vendor contract outside delegated signing authority, and no work may begin before signature.

Access and Data Handling
Vendor access to firm systems must be provisioned through AuthSSO with least privilege and a defined expiry. Shared credentials are prohibited. Vendors may receive only the minimum data needed for the service, and any vendor handling client records must store them in approved environments such as DocVault. Technology reviews vendor access lists every quarter.

Ongoing Monitoring
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed quarterly, Tier 2 vendors annually, and Tier 3 vendors every two years. Reviews cover service level performance, incidents, audit findings, financial condition, and changes in ownership or subcontractors. Results are reported to the Vendor Oversight Review, and material concerns are escalated to the CEO.

Incident Management
Any vendor-related outage, data exposure, or control failure must be reported in #incidents immediately and logged by the Business Owner. Technology leads technical triage, and Compliance determines whether regulatory notification is required. A post-incident review is required for every Tier 1 vendor incident.

Offboarding
When a relationship ends, the Business Owner coordinates revocation of all access within one business day, confirmation of data return or deletion, final invoice reconciliation with Finance, and updates to the vendor register and system dependency records.

Exceptions
Exceptions require written approval from the COO and the Head of Risk, with Compliance consulted where regulatory exposure exists. Exceptions expire after 90 days unless renewed.

Policy Review
This policy is reviewed annually by the COO and approved by the CEO. Questions should be directed to the COO's office.
